bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash balance sheet: net debt shown as (151) in FY24, (292) in FY25 and (206) Cr in FY26 - i.e. negative net debt in all three years - with zero current borrowings on the FY26 and FY25 balance sheet.
- Net worth built from Rs 2,001 Cr (FY24) to Rs 2,098 Cr (FY25) to Rs 2,206 Cr (FY26), funded internally; cash generated from operations of Rs 302 Cr, Rs 464 Cr and Rs 415 Cr over the same years.
- Credit profile of ICRA AA (long term) and A1+ (short term) is listed as a key strength under "Financial Resilience with Strong Credit Profile".
- Returns have compressed over the period shown: ROE 10.4% (FY24), 8.3% (FY25), 8.3% (FY26); ROCE 14.7%, 12.0%, 12.1%; fixed asset turnover 2.5x, 2.3x, 2.2x; current ratio 2.4x, 2.7x, 2.3x.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest footwear manufacturer in India with more than five decades of operating history and over four decades of experience in manufacturing and marketing footwear
- Portfolio of four leading brands — Relaxo, Sparx, Flite and Bahamas — described as leaders in their space, giving a diversified brand platform against competitive threats
- PAN India distribution footprint spanning distributors, retailers, 420 Exclusive Brand Outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and modern trade
- In-house manufacturing across 9 State of the Art facilities in Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand, supporting quality products at affordable prices
- Debt-free balance sheet position — no term loan outstanding as on March 31, 2026 — with capital expenditure funded through internal accruals
- Export franchise recognised with the No. 1 Exporter Award in the Non-Leather Footwear category from the Council for Leather Exports and Star Export House status from the Federation of Indian Export Organisations
- Ongoing investment in R&D and design, with research and development expenditure of ₹21.92 Crores in FY26
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competition from a large unorganised sector and from global brands — The unorganised sector still accounts for approximately 65% of the Indian footwear market as of 2025, dominated by small-scale manufacturers and local artisans who often operate without formal compliance, quality standards or modern infrastructure — making it hard for organised players to compete on price given their higher compliance and operating costs. Competition from global brands is simultaneously intensifying, particularly in the premium and athleisure segments where Relaxo is trying to premiumise.
- Input cost volatility in rubber and synthetic raw materials — The business remains exposed to fluctuations in key raw materials such as Rubber and synthetics including EVA, PU, PVC, LDPE, SBR and POE, which directly impact production costs and margins. The Board's Report also cites volatile raw material prices among the year's headwinds.
- Labour intensity, skilled-worker shortage and rising labour costs — The industry is heavily labour intensive and faces a shortage of skilled workers, especially in advanced design and mechanised operations, which affects productivity and product quality. Dependence on manual labour makes scaling up difficult and limits output consistency, while rising labour costs and a lack of formal training infrastructure compound the problem. Company-level attrition is elevated — permanent employee turnover of 19.84% and permanent worker turnover of 22.48% in FY26, both up from FY25.
- Working-capital blockage from the GST inverted duty structure — Continued accumulation of input tax credit under the inverted duty structure results in significant blockage of working capital. GST refunds are available only for credit on input goods; credit attributable to input services and capital goods remains ineligible for refund, creating a permanent tax cost and cash-flow blockage. Management calls it a key concern requiring policy intervention, and it disproportionately affects manufacturers with substantial service and capital expenditure requirements.
- Foreign exchange exposure on imported inputs and exports — Financial performance is subject to foreign exchange fluctuations given exposure to imported raw materials and export markets. Foreign exchange outflow exceeds inflow, so the Company runs a net forex outflow position.
- Single-segment, single-category concentration — The Company reports only one segment, 'Footwear and related products', and the BRSR shows 99.61% of turnover from manufacture of footwear (NIC 1520). There is no diversification cushion if footwear demand or the affordable/open-footwear categories weaken — a risk demonstrated in FY26 when demand conditions remained challenging through the first half of the year.
- Infrastructure and logistics constraints limiting expansion into smaller markets — Infrastructure constraints, including limitations in logistics and manufacturing capabilities in certain regions, may impact efficiency and scalability, especially in the context of expanding into Tier II, Tier III and rural markets — the very geographies the Company's distribution-deepening strategy targets.
- Under-investment in R&D and design capability across the industry — Relatively lower levels of investment in research & development and design capabilities across the industry may limit the ability to develop globally competitive products, thereby impacting long-term growth in premium segments and export markets — directly relevant to Relaxo's stated premiumisation and export-expansion strategy.
- Disputed indirect-tax and statutory dues across multiple states — The auditor's annexure discloses statutory dues not deposited on account of disputes as at March 31, 2026, spanning purchase tax, VAT/input tax, central excise penalty and GST matters pending before Joint, Additional and Deputy Commissioners, the Delhi Appellate Tribunal and Commissioner (Appeals) across Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Gujarat.

- [Industry - category] Sports & athleisure is called the fastest-growing footwear category, expected to expand at ~10% CAGR; women's footwear is gaining share; India has moved from the 6th to the 5th largest footwear exporter by quantity.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded 129 bps YoY to 12.9% in Q2FY26 due to cost rationalization, back-end optimization, and full GST price pass-through; no margin compression from inverted duty structure expected as refund mechanism covers bulk impact
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: expected to turn positive in Q4FY26; margin: stable to expand; order inflow: not guided; capex/commissioning: INR100-150 crores FY26-FY27 for warehouse modernization, HO building, and operational efficiency - no capacity expansion planned
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Premiumization via Flite PU and athleisure sneakers; potential market share gain from unorganized sector due to GST 5% pricing advantage; RPA app driving 60% of secondary sales
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen sales capability by expanding the distribution network, onboarding new distributors and deepening market penetration and reach across geographies
- Improve inventory management and working capital efficiency, including a pilot of a new Warehouse Management System that dispatches curated size assortments to distributors instead of conventional standard pack configurations
- Deepen distributor and retailer engagement through digital tools such as the Relaxo Parivaar App and over 100 retailer meets in General Trade and Multi-Brand Outlets
- Invest in brand building and product innovation — a new brand ambassador and the 'Sar Utha Kadam Badha' campaign for Flite, and over 250 trend-forward designs added across categories
- Optimise the retail (EBO) portfolio: open new stores in strategic locations while closing underperforming ones, and improve assortment, price points and store-team capability
- Scale e-commerce, quick commerce and modern trade through direct platform partnerships and activation of direct 3P operations, backed by supply-chain infrastructure enhancements
- Expand internationally — deepen brand equity in established territories while entering high-potential emerging markets, most notably across the African continent, supported by the Dubai branch office
- Focus on innovation, premium products and customer-centric practices to strengthen the Company's position in the Indian footwear market
- Invest in energy-efficient technology and alternate energy at plants, including rooftop solar and biomass boilers, to reduce cost of production
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Relaxo manufactures at 9 State of the Art footwear facilities across Bahadurgarh (Haryana), Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) and Haridwar (Uttarakhand); the BRSR reports 10 national plants (a count that includes the Company-owned warehouse at Lovakhurd) and one national office, plus one international office, being the Dubai branch that strategises export plans and expansion into newer geographies. The Annual Report does not describe any new plant, greenfield project or capacity-addition programme with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion during FY26 was footprint-, channel- and efficiency-led rather than capacity-led: the Company opened 35 new Exclusive Brand Outlets in strategic locations while closing 33 underperforming ones, ending with 420 outlets as of March 31, 2026; expanded its distribution network by onboarding new distributors; piloted a new Warehouse Management System enabling dispatch of curated size assortments to distributors; scaled quick commerce through direct platform partnerships and activated direct 3P e-commerce operations; and entered high-potential emerging markets, most notably across the African continent, taking its international presence to over 35 countries across six continents (37 countries per the BRSR). On the plant side the Company invested in energy and technology upgrades rather than new lines — installing biomass boilers at RFL III and RFL X to save fuel cost, LED lighting at the Baproda warehouse, an energy-efficient I-4 compressor with VFD, temperature cut-off units on cooling-tower motors, and 6 MW of rooftop solar across its units in Haryana, Bhiwadi and Uttarakhand with an expected payback period of 3 years; it also continued replacing old manual machinery with energy-efficient automatic machines. Management states that the capital expenditure incurred during FY26 was in line with the Company's growth strategy and was funded through internal accruals, with no term loan outstanding as on March 31, 2026, and that research and development expenditure was ₹21.92 Crores.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Long-term fundamentals of the Indian footwear industry remain deeply promising; the organised segment's share of the market is set to expand meaningfully over the coming decade, benefiting players with strong brands, quality manufacturing and wide distribution reach
- Demand conditions were challenging during the first half of FY26, but strong momentum in the fourth quarter provides a foundation management says supports consistent growth and improving profitability
- Premiumisation: the premium segment accounted for 54% of Indian market value in FY25, with average selling prices rising from ₹219 in FY15 to ₹344 in FY25 and women's footwear ASPs from ₹192 to ₹332
- Low per-capita consumption in India at 1.9 pairs annually versus a global average of 3.2 pairs, highlighting a significant long-term growth opportunity
- Sports & Athleisure is the fastest-growing category in Indian footwear, estimated to grow at a CAGR of approximately 11.8%, driven by Gen-Z sneaker culture and fitness-conscious lifestyles
- Growth of e-commerce, quick commerce and omni-channel formats, with 85% of Indian footwear purchases still offline as of FY25 and the online channel's trajectory consistently upward
- Formalisation of the sector, BIS quality standards and GST rationalisation supporting the organised segment; supply-chain diversification away from China creating an export opportunity for India, the fifth largest global footwear exporter by volume
- Category-level tailwinds in women's footwear from rising workforce participation, and continued long-term potential in children's footwear
- Rising Indian disposable incomes and a rapidly expanding middle class underpinning consumption; India cementing its position as the 4th largest economy and targeting 3rd within a few years
- Margin/cost levers cited by management: focused market initiatives, enhanced channel engagement and prudent cost management, plus energy-conservation measures at plants to mitigate rising energy costs and reduce cost of production
- Headwinds flagged: input cost volatility in Rubber and synthetics (EVA, PU, PVC, LDPE, SBR, POE), forex fluctuation, an unorganised sector still at approximately 65% of the market, intensifying competition from global brands in premium and athleisure, skilled-labour shortage and rising labour costs, and working-capital blockage from the inverted duty structure
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Revenue declined due to GST 12%->5% transition causing channel destocking, but EBITDA and PAT margins expanded due to cost control and full price pass-through; recovery expected from Q4FY26 as inventory clears and GST benefits fully flow through to consumers.

open.item: The Company successfully piloted a new Warehouse Management System enabling dispatch of curated size assortments to distributors, enhancing distribution capability and supply-chain agility.

open.horizon: FY26 final dividend, payable after AGM on 24 September 2026
open.item: The Board has recommended a final dividend of 350%, equivalent to ₹3.50 per equity share of ₹1 each fully paid up, for FY26, to be declared at the 42nd AGM.

The Company will build on portfolio expansion and supply-chain enhancements to deliver sustained growth, improved speed and greater fulfilment efficiency in e-commerce and quick commerce in the coming year.

The unspent CSR balance of ₹454.89 lacs transferred to the Unspent CSR Account on April 29, 2026 will be spent on Education & Skill Development and Environment Conservation & Health projects approved by the Board.
The Company intends to grow overall exports through participation in international exhibitions and its operational Dubai branch office, expanding into newer geographies.

Management flags the continued accumulation of input tax credit under the inverted duty structure as a key concern blocking working capital and creating permanent tax cost, requiring policy intervention.
The Company is deepening brand equity in established export territories while executing strategic entries into high-potential emerging markets, most notably across the African continent.
The Company aims to further strengthen its position in the Indian footwear market by continuing to focus on innovation, premium products and customer-centric practices.

currentContext.expansion: Relaxo manufactures at 9 State of the Art footwear facilities across Bahadurgarh (Haryana), Bhiwadi (Rajasthan) and Haridwar (Uttarakhand); the BRSR reports 10 national plants (a count that includes the Company-owned warehouse at Lovakhurd) and one national office, plus one international office, being the Dubai branch that strategises export plans and expansion into newer geographies. The Annual Report does not describe any new plant, greenfield project or capacity-addition programme with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Expansion during FY26 was footprint-, channel- and efficiency-led rather than capacity-led: the Company opened 35 new Exclusive Brand Outlets in strategic locations while closing 33 underperforming ones, ending with 420 outlets as of March 31, 2026; expanded its distribution network by onboarding new distributors; piloted a new Warehouse Management System enabling dispatch of curated size assortments to distributors; scaled quick commerce through direct platform partnerships and activated direct 3P e-commerce operations; and entered high-potential emerging markets, most notably across the African continent, taking its international presence to over 35 countries across six continents (37 countries per the BRSR). On the plant side the Company invested in energy and technology upgrades rather than new lines — installing biomass boilers at RFL III and RFL X to save fuel cost, LED lighting at the Baproda warehouse, an energy-efficient I-4 compressor with VFD, temperature cut-off units on cooling-tower motors, and 6 MW of rooftop solar across its units in Haryana, Bhiwadi and Uttarakhand with an expected payback period of 3 years; it also continued replacing old manual machinery with energy-efficient automatic machines. Management states that the capital expenditure incurred during FY26 was in line with the Company's growth strategy and was funded through internal accruals, with no term loan outstanding as on March 31, 2026, and that research and development expenditure was ₹21.92 Crores.

risks.risk: Competition from a large unorganised sector and from global brands
risks.note: The unorganised sector still accounts for approximately 65% of the Indian footwear market as of 2025, dominated by small-scale manufacturers and local artisans who often operate without formal compliance, quality standards or modern infrastructure — making it hard for organised players to compete on price given their higher compliance and operating costs. Competition from global brands is simultaneously intensifying, particularly in the premium and athleisure segments where Relaxo is trying to premiumise.

risks.risk: Input cost volatility in rubber and synthetic raw materials
risks.note: The business remains exposed to fluctuations in key raw materials such as Rubber and synthetics including EVA, PU, PVC, LDPE, SBR and POE, which directly impact production costs and margins. The Board's Report also cites volatile raw material prices among the year's headwinds.

risks.risk: Labour intensity, skilled-worker shortage and rising labour costs
risks.note: The industry is heavily labour intensive and faces a shortage of skilled workers, especially in advanced design and mechanised operations, which affects productivity and product quality. Dependence on manual labour makes scaling up difficult and limits output consistency, while rising labour costs and a lack of formal training infrastructure compound the problem. Company-level attrition is elevated — permanent employee turnover of 19.84% and permanent worker turnover of 22.48% in FY26, both up from FY25.

risks.risk: Working-capital blockage from the GST inverted duty structure
risks.note: Continued accumulation of input tax credit under the inverted duty structure results in significant blockage of working capital. GST refunds are available only for credit on input goods; credit attributable to input services and capital goods remains ineligible for refund, creating a permanent tax cost and cash-flow blockage. Management calls it a key concern requiring policy intervention, and it disproportionately affects manufacturers with substantial service and capital expenditure requirements.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imported inputs and exports
risks.note: Financial performance is subject to foreign exchange fluctuations given exposure to imported raw materials and export markets. Foreign exchange outflow exceeds inflow, so the Company runs a net forex outflow position.

The Company reports only one segment, 'Footwear and related products', and the BRSR shows 99.61% of turnover from manufacture of footwear (NIC 1520). There is no diversification cushion if footwear demand or the affordable/open-footwear categories weaken — a risk demonstrated in FY26 when demand conditions remained challenging through the first half of the year.

risks.risk: Infrastructure and logistics constraints limiting expansion into smaller markets
risks.note: Infrastructure constraints, including limitations in logistics and manufacturing capabilities in certain regions, may impact efficiency and scalability, especially in the context of expanding into Tier II, Tier III and rural markets — the very geographies the Company's distribution-deepening strategy targets.

risks.risk: Under-investment in R&D and design capability across the industry
risks.note: Relatively lower levels of investment in research & development and design capabilities across the industry may limit the ability to develop globally competitive products, thereby impacting long-term growth in premium segments and export markets — directly relevant to Relaxo's stated premiumisation and export-expansion strategy.

risks.risk: Disputed indirect-tax and statutory dues across multiple states
risks.note: The auditor's annexure discloses statutory dues not deposited on account of disputes as at March 31, 2026, spanning purchase tax, VAT/input tax, central excise penalty and GST matters pending before Joint, Additional and Deputy Commissioners, the Delhi Appellate Tribunal and Commissioner (Appeals) across Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Gujarat.

one-line thesis: Revenue declined due to GST 12%->5% transition causing channel destocking, but EBITDA and PAT margins expanded due to cost control and full price pass-through; recovery expected from Q4FY26 as inventory clears and GST benefits fully flow through to consumers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Long-term fundamentals of the Indian footwear industry remain deeply promising; the organised segment's share of the market is set to expand meaningfully over the coming decade, benefiting players with strong brands, quality manufacturing and wide distribution reach
- Demand conditions were challenging during the first half of FY26, but strong momentum in the fourth quarter provides a foundation management says supports consistent growth and improving profitability
- Premiumisation: the premium segment accounted for 54% of Indian market value in FY25, with average selling prices rising from ₹219 in FY15 to ₹344 in FY25 and women's footwear ASPs from ₹192 to ₹332
- Low per-capita consumption in India at 1.9 pairs annually versus a global average of 3.2 pairs, highlighting a significant long-term growth opportunity
- Sports & Athleisure is the fastest-growing category in Indian footwear, estimated to grow at a CAGR of approximately 11.8%, driven by Gen-Z sneaker culture and fitness-conscious lifestyles
- Growth of e-commerce, quick commerce and omni-channel formats, with 85% of Indian footwear purchases still offline as of FY25 and the online channel's trajectory consistently upward
- Formalisation of the sector, BIS quality standards and GST rationalisation supporting the organised segment; supply-chain diversification away from China creating an export opportunity for India, the fifth largest global footwear exporter by volume
- Category-level tailwinds in women's footwear from rising workforce participation, and continued long-term potential in children's footwear
- Rising Indian disposable incomes and a rapidly expanding middle class underpinning consumption; India cementing its position as the 4th largest economy and targeting 3rd within a few years
- Margin/cost levers cited by management: focused market initiatives, enhanced channel engagement and prudent cost management, plus energy-conservation measures at plants to mitigate rising energy costs and reduce cost of production
- Headwinds flagged: input cost volatility in Rubber and synthetics (EVA, PU, PVC, LDPE, SBR, POE), forex fluctuation, an unorganised sector still at approximately 65% of the market, intensifying competition from global brands in premium and athleisure, skilled-labour shortage and rising labour costs, and working-capital blockage from the inverted duty structure

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Industry] The deck cites industry reports for the Indian footwear market growing at 9.7% CAGR from Rs 1,927 Bn in 2025 to Rs 4,433 Bn by 2034, and the global market at 4.5% CAGR from $477 Bn (2025) to $676 Bn (2033).
- [Industry - formalisation] India's organised share of footwear is projected to rise from 35% in 2025 to 45% by 2034, with the organised market growing at 13% CAGR from Rs 674 Bn in 2025 to Rs 1,995 Bn by 2034.
- [Industry - category] Sports & athleisure is called the fastest-growing footwear category, expected to expand at ~10% CAGR; women's footwear is gaining share; India has moved from the 6th to the 5th largest footwear exporter by quantity.
- [Market data as on 30 June 2026] Market cap Rs 10,100.68 Cr, enterprise value Rs 10,096 Cr, free float 28.73%, shares outstanding 24.89 Cr, 52-week high Rs 518.85 and low Rs 237.90, 3M ADTV 12,56,177 shares, 52-week ADTV Rs 23.0 Cr, total shareholders 2,23,844.

one-line thesis: Revenue declined due to GST 12%->5% transition causing channel destocking, but EBITDA and PAT margins expanded due to cost control and full price pass-through; recovery expected from Q4FY26 as inventory clears and GST benefits fully flow through to consumers.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -7.5% YoY (Q2FY26); EBITDA: -3.2% YoY, margin +129 bps to 12.9%; PAT: -2.7% YoY, margin +34 bps to 5.8%; order book: not disclosed; net debt: not disclosed - no one-offs or accounting distortions noted except for higher other income from treasury/hedging gains
guidance: Revenue growth: expected to turn positive in Q4FY26; margin: stable to expand; order inflow: not guided; capex/commissioning: INR100-150 crores FY26-FY27 for warehouse modernization, HO building, and operational efficiency - no capacity expansion planned
segment / subsidiary detail: Open footwear: 80% of sales; Closed footwear: 20% of sales; >98% of portfolio priced below INR2,500; >90% below INR1,000; Flite brand launching premium PU range; Sparx and Bahamas contribute 65% combined
growth verticals / optionality: Premiumization via Flite PU and athleisure sneakers; potential market share gain from unorganized sector due to GST 5% pricing advantage; RPA app driving 60% of secondary sales
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 129 bps YoY to 12.9% in Q2FY26 due to cost rationalization, back-end optimization, and full GST price pass-through; no margin compression from inverted duty structure expected as refund mechanism covers bulk impact
capex / expansion: INR100-150 crores for FY26-FY27; focused on warehouse modernization, HO building, moulds, plant renovations; no capacity expansion planned for next 18 months
capital allocation: Capex prioritized for operational efficiency over capacity expansion; no dividend or buyback guidance provided; focus on debt reduction and working capital optimization
risks & watch-items: Delayed inventory digestion beyond December 2025; inverted duty structure refund delays; persistent unorganized competition; consumer sentiment remains muted; regional variation in GST adoption speed
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; confident in GST 2.0 tailwinds; acknowledge near-term headwinds from channel destocking but expect recovery from Q4FY26; emphasize competitive positioning and cost discipline
non-obvious takeaways: Distributor trade discount remains fixed at 9% of wholesale price (not MRP), so absolute commission falls with lower MRP - but management believes volume growth offsets this; RPA app now drives 60% of secondary sales, indicating digital transformation is accelerating
